name: Glycolysis
summary: Cytosol, every cell. Glucose → 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP + 2 NADH. Everything from glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate on runs twice per glucose. Irreversible (and regulated): hexokinase/glucokinase, PFK-1, pyruvate kinase.

g6p.name: Glucose-6-phosphate
g6p.notes: Branch point: → pentose phosphate pathway (G6PD), → glycogen (via phosphoglucomutase to G1P), → free glucose in liver (glucose-6-phosphatase). Inhibits hexokinase.

f6p.name: Fructose-6-phosphate
f6p.notes: Also the substrate for PFK-2, which makes fructose-2,6-bisphosphate (the main activator of PFK-1).

dhap.name: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate
dhap.notes: Also reduced to glycerol-3-phosphate for triglyceride and phospholipid synthesis.

g3p.name: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
g3p.notes: Two per glucose (one from aldolase, one via TPI), so every later step runs twice.

bpg13.name: 1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate
bpg13.notes: High-energy acyl phosphate. In RBCs, bisphosphoglycerate mutase diverts it to 2,3-BPG (shifts the O₂ curve right), skipping the PGK ATP.

pg3.name: 3-Phosphoglycerate
pg3.notes: Precursor for serine (and from it glycine, cysteine).

pyruvate.name: Pyruvate
pyruvate.notes: Fates: lactate (LDH, regenerates NAD⁺), acetyl-CoA (PDH), oxaloacetate (pyruvate carboxylase), alanine (ALT).

hk.name: Hexokinase / Glucokinase
hk.notes: Hexokinase: most tissues, low Km / low Vmax, inhibited by G6P. Glucokinase: liver and pancreatic β cells, high Km / high Vmax, induced by insulin, held in the nucleus by GKRP (F6P promotes binding). Glucokinase mutations → MODY2. Gluconeogenic bypass: glucose-6-phosphatase.

pfk1.name: Phosphofructokinase-1
pfk1.notes: Rate-limiting, committed step. Activated by AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate; inhibited by ATP and citrate. Gluconeogenic bypass: fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase.

aldolase.name: Aldolase
aldolase.notes: Splits one 6-carbon sugar into two trioses: DHAP + G3P. Aldolase B (liver) also cleaves fructose-1-phosphate — its deficiency is hereditary fructose intolerance.

tpi.name: Triose phosphate isomerase
tpi.notes: Converts DHAP to G3P so both halves of glucose continue down the pathway. Reversible.

gapdh.name: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase
gapdh.notes: The only oxidation in glycolysis: makes NADH and adds inorganic phosphate (not from ATP) to form high-energy 1,3-BPG. Arsenate substitutes for Pi and bypasses the PGK ATP.

pgk.name: Phosphoglycerate kinase
pgk.notes: First substrate-level phosphorylation (2 ATP per glucose). Reversible despite the name 'kinase'.

pgm.name: Phosphoglycerate mutase
pgm.notes: Moves the phosphate from C3 to C2. Not to be confused with phosphoglucomutase (G6P ⇌ G1P, glycogen).

enolase.name: Enolase
enolase.notes: Dehydration (releases H₂O) creating the enol phosphate. Inhibited by fluoride.

pk.name: Pyruvate kinase
pk.notes: Second substrate-level phosphorylation. Activated by F1,6BP (feed-forward); inhibited by ATP and alanine; liver isoform inactivated by glucagon (PKA phosphorylation). Deficiency → hemolytic anemia (most common glycolytic enzyme defect). Gluconeogenic bypass: pyruvate carboxylase + PEPCK.
